reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only discusses general HEA properties, lightweight HEA design challenges, and the influence of Mg content on phases and corrosion, without providing specific prior observations that a metastable solid solution decomposes into passivation-promoting intermetallics upon heat treatment, nor that such intermetallics improve high-temperature oxidation. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight HEA can be initially a metastable single-phase solid solution
Post-processing heat treatment can decompose this solid solution into fine intermetallic phases
Resulting intermetallic phases promote localized formation of passivating oxide layers (e.g., Ti/Zn oxides)
These passivating layers lower corrosion current density and improve high-temperature oxidation resistance
Sluggish diffusion in HEAs influences this phase evolution and passivation process
